device.model: RFSoC board with a QICK tProc-v2 processor
device.name: QICK RFSoC instrument (QICKoDeS QCoDeS driver)

facts.text: QickInstrument is a QCoDeS Instrument whose constructor takes ns_host and ns_port=8888
The constructor obtains soc, the Pyro4 proxy of the QickSoc, and soccfg from make_proxy(ns_host, ns_port)
It asserts exactly one tProc of type qick_processor and refuses any other type
It builds StandardDacChannel or MultiplexedDacChannel objects from soccfg['gens'] and AdcChannel objects from soccfg['readouts']
hard_avgs is a ManualParameter with vals=Ints(min_value=0) and initial value 1000
soft_avgs is a ManualParameter with vals=Ints(min_value=0) and initial value 1
final_delay is a SweepableParameter with unit sec, initial value 1e-6 and min_value=0
final_wait is a SweepableParameter with unit sec, initial value 0 and min_value=0
initial_delay is a SweepableParameter with unit sec, initial value 1e-6 and min_value=0
SweepableParameter.get_raw returns the stored QickParam rounded value, or its start for a scalar, and SweepableParameter.set_raw stores the value as a QickParam and registers or removes a sweep
set_macro_list replaces the macro_list ChannelTuple with the given sequence of Macro objects
run refuses an empty macro_list with a RuntimeError that asks for set_macro_list first
run takes a qcodes Measurement and returns the datasaver run_id, writing the acquired data to the QCoDeS dataset
run_without_saving builds an AveragerProgram, acquires through qick.qick_asm.AcquireMixin, and returns a dict of complex IQ values keyed by readout name
The DDR4 num_transfers parameter is a ManualParameter with vals=Ints(min_value=1)
get_idn reports vendor Xilinx, the soccfg board name, no serial, and the remote and local QICK versions
The project depends on pyro4, qcodes and qick>=0.2.255 and requires Python 3.11 or newer
The README instructs the operator to start the Pyro4 nameserver on port 8888 and the QICK server on a Xilinx board before constructing QickInstrument with the board address

safe_state.description: No safe state is certified: the e-stop clears the instrument's macro list, so no new run of this object can start, and reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; a program already running on the board and an armed DDR4 buffer continue, because the pinned upstream has no stop, abort or disarm method
